name: sensor-etl
runtime: Node.js 24, no npm dependencies, tests with the built-in node:test runner

features.name: Ingest CSV exports into one JSON file per day with count, min, max and avg per sensor
Daily buckets follow the Asia/Seoul calendar day (UTC+9)
Idempotent ingest: a second run on the same input leaves the output byte-identical
Malformed rows are skipped, listed in <out>/rejected.csv with a reason and counted in the summary line
features.documented_in: README.md, section "Rejected rows"; CLI help (node bin/sensor-etl.js --help)

features.name: Sensor names are arbitrary UTF-8 text and every distinct name is its own key
Report of the stored aggregates as tab-separated text
Exit status: 0 also for a run without input files, 1 for usage errors, 2 for a missing input or output directory
features.documented_in: README.md, sections "Usage" and "Exit status"; CLI help

features.name: Input tolerance: LF or CRLF line endings, blank lines, whitespace around fields, files without the header are skipped with a warning

defects.title: Readings are bucketed by their UTC date instead of the Asia/Seoul calendar day
defects.requirement_quote: Daily buckets use the Asia/Seoul calendar day (UTC+9, no daylight saving).
defects.expected: daily/2026-09-02.json: 2026-09-01T15:30:00Z is 00:30 on 2 September in Asia/Seoul, so the reading belongs to the 2026-09-02 bucket (the README gives the same example with 15:00:00Z).
defects.actual: daily/2026-09-01.json: the reading is filed under its UTC date. Every reading taken between 15:00Z and 23:59Z ends up in the file of the previous Seoul day, independent of the TZ setting of the machine.

defects.title: A second ingest run on the same input double counts: every count in the daily files is added again
defects.requirement_quote: Ingest is idempotent: running it again on the same input leaves the output byte-identical.
defects.expected: diff prints nothing and exits 0: after the second run daily/2026-09-01.json and daily/2026-09-02.json are byte-identical to the result of the first run.
defects.actual: Both daily files change. Every count is doubled (2026-09-01: humidity-1 count 2 -> 4, temp-1 count 3 -> 6; 2026-09-02: both counts 2 -> 4) while min, max and avg stay the same; each further run adds the counts once more. Ingest merges the batch into the stored daily files without knowing that it has already been ingested.

defects.title: Rejected rows are counted in the summary line but <out>/rejected.csv is never written
defects.requirement_quote: Malformed rows are skipped, written to `<out>/rejected.csv` with a reason, and counted in the summary line as `rejected=<n>`.
defects.expected: The summary line reports rejected=3 and /tmp/sensor-etl-d3/out/rejected.csv exists with the header file,line,reason,row followed by three lines: a.csv,3,unparseable timestamp,... / a.csv,4,non-numeric value,... / a.csv,5,wrong column count,...
defects.actual: The summary line is 'ingested files=1 rows=4 accepted=1 rejected=3 days=1', but the output directory only contains daily/. rejected.csv does not exist (cat: No such file or directory). A rejected.csv left over from an earlier run is even removed.

defects.title: Non-ASCII characters are stripped from sensor names, so different Korean-named sensors are merged into one key
defects.requirement_quote: Korean names such as `온도-1` are allowed, and different names are different keys.
defects.expected: daily/2026-09-01.json has two keys: "습도-1" with {"count":1,"min":55,"max":55,"avg":55} and "온도-1" with {"count":1,"min":21.5,"max":21.5,"avg":21.5}.
defects.actual: daily/2026-09-01.json has the single key "-1" with {"count":2,"min":21.5,"max":55,"avg":38.25}: the Korean characters are removed from both names and a temperature and a humidity sensor are aggregated together. Names that consist only of non-ASCII characters (온도, 습도) all end up under the empty key "".

traps.description: An input directory that exists but holds no *.csv file makes ingest print "no input files" and exit 0 without creating the output directory. This can look like a silently swallowed error, but it is the documented behaviour (README sections "Usage" and "Exit status", CLI help, and the message of the commit "fix: exit with status 2 when the input directory is missing"). Only a missing directory is an error (exit 2).
traps.correct_behaviour: stdout is exactly "no input files", the exit status is 0 and nothing is written.
traps.check: d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir "$d/in" && node bin/sensor-etl.js ingest --in "$d/in" --out "$d/out"; echo "exit=$?"; ls "$d"

traps.description: CRLF line endings. The history contains "fix: accept CRLF line endings" and the parser was touched again afterwards ("refactor: let the parser tag rejected rows with their file"), which invites the suspicion of a regression. CRLF input is still ingested completely: no row is rejected and the output equals the one for LF input.
traps.correct_behaviour: The summary line is "ingested files=1 rows=2 accepted=2 rejected=0 days=1" and daily/2026-09-01.json contains "temp-1": {"count":2,"min":21.5,"max":22,"avg":21.75}, exactly as for the same rows with LF endings.
traps.check:
d=$(mktemp -d) && mkdir "$d/in" && printf 'sensor,timestamp,value
temp-1,2026-09-01T03:00:00Z,21.5
temp-1,2026-09-01T04:00:00Z,22
' > "$d/in/a.csv" && node bin/sensor-etl.js ingest --in "$d/in" --out "$d/out" && cat "$d/out/daily/2026-09-01.json"

history_signals.commit_subject: perf: merge into existing daily files
history_signals.why_it_matters: The most recent functional change. It replaces the rebuild of daily/ with a merge into the files of earlier runs but does not track which input has already been ingested, which introduces D2 while the README still promises idempotent re-runs. The only test it adds covers mergeStats in isolation.
Presented as a pure refactoring of dayKey, but the diff also drops the 9 hour shift to Asia/Seoul, which introduces D1. No test uses a timestamp between 15:00Z and 24:00Z, so the suite stays green.

history_signals.commit_subject: fix: drop control characters from sensor names
history_signals.why_it_matters: Adds sensorKey(), which keeps printable ASCII characters only and therefore introduces D4. The tests added with it use ASCII names only.

history_signals.commit_subject: refactor: let the parser tag rejected rows with their file
history_signals.why_it_matters: Rewrites the ingest loop: the destructured `rejected` now shadows the list that is passed to writeRejected, and the line that filled that list is removed. This introduces D3; lint is node --check only and does not report the shadowing.

history_signals.commit_subject: feat: write malformed rows to rejected.csv
history_signals.why_it_matters: Introduces the rejected.csv requirement together with its tests (parser reasons, the writer function in isolation, the rejected=<n> count). None of them looks at the file after an ingest run, which is why D3 goes unnoticed.
Trap T2: a past fix in a file that later commits changed again. CRLF input still works and must not be reported as a regression.

history_signals.commit_subject: fix: exit with status 2 when the input directory is missing
history_signals.why_it_matters: Trap T1: the message states that an existing directory without CSV files is not an error (prints "no input files", exit 0), while a missing directory exits 2.

what_ci_runs: make lint: node --check on bin/*.js, lib/*.js and test/*.js (syntax check only)
make test: node --test, 29 tests in test/*.test.js (unit tests for decimal, timeutil, csv, aggregate and rejects, plus CLI smoke tests that each run once against a fresh temporary directory)
what_ci_does_not_cover: No test uses a timestamp between 15:00Z and 23:59Z, where the UTC day and the Asia/Seoul day differ (D1)
No test runs ingest twice against the same output directory, so idempotency is never checked (D2)
No test looks for <out>/rejected.csv after an ingest run; only the parser, the writer function in isolation and the rejected=<n> count are tested (D3)
No test uses a non-ASCII sensor name (D4)
Lint is node --check only; there is no static analysis that would report the shadowed variable behind D3
The Jenkins pipeline (docker agent node:24-bookworm) only wraps make lint test, which can be run locally as it is
